I will keep my land in the usual wheat-maize rotation, because that is the safest and steadiest way for me to farm in Quzhou County. Our area is suited to winter wheat followed by summer maize, and at my age I would rather choose crops I know well, that sell easily, and that fit the local water and labor conditions. I will not spread myself across too many crops, because that makes field work, buying inputs, and pest control harder. I will use improved seed for wheat because it is stable and familiar, and hybrid seed for maize because the yield is better. I will manage fertilizer in a moderate way, not too little and not too much, because I want steady output and I do not want to waste money. For tillage, I will use rotary tillage because it matches the machinery and habits I can manage. I will irrigate wheat more than maize, since wheat needs water at key stages in our area, while maize can rely more on summer rain with only limited extra watering if needed. I will also spray pesticides only as needed for the common weeds, insects, and diseases, because I want to protect yield but keep costs under control.
